chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basri, from Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Abu Nu'aym, from the doorkeeper of Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad:

When the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was brought, he ordered it placed before him in a gold basin and began striking his front teeth with a stick, saying: "Grey hair hastened to you, O Abu Abdillah." A man said: "Stop! I saw the Messenger of God kissing where you place your stick." He said: "A day for the day of Badr." Then Ali ibn al-Husayn was shackled and taken with the women and captives to prison, and I was with them. We passed no alleyway except that we found it full of men and women hitting their faces and weeping.
They were imprisoned and it was made narrow for them. Then Ibn Ziyad (la) called for Ali ibn al-Husayn and the women, and the head of al-Husayn was present.

Zaynab bint Ali (as) was among them. Ibn Ziyad said: "Praise be to Allah who has exposed you, killed you, and belied your narrations." Zaynab said: "Praise be to Allah who ennobled us with Muhammad and purified us with a thorough purification. Allah only exposes the transgressor and belies the wretched." He said: "How do you see what Allah has done with you, the Ahl al-Bayt?" She said: "Being killed had been ordained for them, so they have gone into their place of rest.
Allah will gather you and them, and you will be judged by Him." Ibn Ziyad (la) became angry and concerned with her. Amr ibn Harith calmed him down.

Zaynab said: "O Ibn Ziyad! What you have perpetrated against us is enough. You have killed our men, cut off our foundation, made our sanctity permissible, and taken our women and children into captivity. If that satisfies you, then you have been made satisfied." Ibn Ziyad ordered them back to jail, and sent the news of the killing of al-Husayn (as) to the frontiers. Then the captives and the head of al-Husayn were taken to the Levant.

A group narrated to me: throughout the nights, they would hear the lament of the Jinn over al-Husayn until the break of dawn. When we entered Damascus, the women and captives were brought in by daylight with their faces uncovered. The cold people of the Levant said: "We have never seen captives more beautiful than these. Who are you?" Sakina bint al-Husayn (as) said: "We are the captives of the Family of Muhammad." They were placed on the stairs of the mosque, and among them was Ali ibn al-Husayn (as), who on that day was a young man. An elder of the Levant came to them and said: "Praise be to Allah who killed you, destroyed you, and cut off the age of sedition." He did not stop insulting them. When he finished, Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) said: "Have you not read the Book of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you not read this verse, 'Say: I do not ask you for a reward for this except that you love those near of kin' [42:23]?" He said: "Of course." He said: "So, we are them." Then he said: "Did you not read, 'And give to those near of kin their right' [17:26]?" He said: "Of course." He said: "So, we are them." He said: "Did you not read this verse: 'Allah only desires to keep the uncleanness away from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification' [33:33]?" He said: "Of course." He said: "So, we are them." So, the Levantine raised his hands to the sky and said three times: "O Allah! I repent to you.

O Allah! For You, I dissociate from the enemy of the Family of Muhammad and the killers of the Ahl al-Bayt of Muhammad. I have read the Quran, but I have never noticed this before today." Then the women of al-Husayn (as) were brought to Yazid ibn Muawiya. The women of the Family of Yazid and the daughters of Muawiya cried out and grieved. The head of al-Husayn was put in front of him.

Sakina said: "By Allah! I have never seen a harder heart than Yazid, nor have I seen a disbeliever or pagan more evil than him." He then called for the head of al-Husayn to be installed at the gate of the Mosque of Damascus. It was reported from Fatima bint Ali (as) that she said: "When we sat before Yazid ibn Muawiya, he was initially kind and gentle to us. Then a red-faced man from the people of the Levant went to him and said: 'O commander of the faithful! Gift me this girl' — meaning me, and I was a beautiful girl at the time. I became terrified, thinking that he would do that. So, I grasped onto the clothes of my sister, who was older and more mature than me. She said: 'You have lied, by Allah, and have become cursed. That is not yours nor his.' So, Yazid (la) became angry and said: 'Rather, you have lied, by Allah, for if I wanted to, I would have done it.' She said: 'No, by Allah, Allah has not made that for you, unless you exit our way and take on a different religion.' So, Yazid (la) became angry and said: 'You speak to me like this?! Your father and your brother exited the religion.' So, she said: 'You, your grandfather, and your father were guided to the religion of Allah and the religion of my brother, my father, and my grandfather.' He said: 'You have lied, enemy of Allah.' She said: 'An oppressive ruler who ravages with his power.' He (la) became humiliated, so he went quiet. So, the Levantine (la) repeated: 'O commander of the faithful! Gift me this girl.' So, he said to him: 'Leave — may Allah gift you a destructive judgment.'"

key_terms.أهل البيت: The People of the House — the Prophet Muhammad's family, specifically Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, as identified by the Verse of Purification (33:33)
key_terms.الرجس: Impurity/uncleanness — from 33:33, that which God removed from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.السبايا: The captives — referring to the women and children of al-Husayn's family taken prisoner after Karbala
key_terms.المودة في القربى: Love for the near relatives — a Quranic obligation from 42:23, interpreted as love for the Prophet's family

ai.seo_question: What happened to the family of Imam al-Husayn after the Battle of Karbala?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the aftermath of the Battle of Karbala (61 AH/680 CE), describing how the head of Imam al-Husayn was desecrated by Ibn Ziyad in Kufa, the imprisonment and transport of the captive women and Ali ibn al-Husayn to Damascus, their public humiliation, and the courageous confrontations of Zaynab and the daughters of the Prophet's family with their captors. A pivotal scene occurs when Ali ibn al-Husayn educates a Syrian elder about the Ahl al-Bayt's identity through Quranic verses (42:23, 17:26, 33:33), leading to the man's repentance. The narrative concludes with the bold exchange between the women and Yazid in his court.
